prs.author: NishchayMahor
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Python's default `Exception.__reduce_ex__` reconstructs exceptions by calling `cls(*self.args)`, but `MCPError`/`McpError` stores only the message string in `self.args` (not the `ErrorData` object), and `UrlElicitationRequiredError.__init__` expects `(elicitations, message)` — not the `(code, message, data)` tuple stored by the parent. prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2703 is the most complete fix: it adds `__reduce__` directly to both the base class (`McpError`, reconstructing from `self.error`) and the subclass (`UrlElicitationRequiredError`, reconstructing from the message string), using the standard Python pickle protocol on each class. PR #2478 uses an indirect helper function (`_restore_mcp_error`) rather than placing `__reduce__` on the classes themselves, which adds indirection and still requires the base-class pickle path to call through the helper. PR #2703's per-class `__reduce__` approach is self-contained, idiomatic, and covers the full inheritance chain.

PR #2703's per-class `__reduce__` approach is self-contained, idiomatic, and covers the full inheritance chain.
